nodes.label: Factorised inductive temporal-then-spatial encoder (Option 1)
nodes.rationale: A strictly inductive temporal-per-node encoder followed by gated inductive spatial message passing, with a direct multi-horizon head and a light per-disease adaptation surface. Factorisation is preferred over STGCN-style interleaving because the diseases do not share a transmission kernel - dengue spreads over short-range vector-suitable geography, Ebola by distance- and population-weighted human movement - so a mis-specified graph is expected, not exceptional. Factorisation quarantines that error in one gated channel; interleaving lets it contaminate the temporal representation at every block.

nodes.label: C2 - no shared-trunk parameter may have a dimension equal to N
nodes.rationale: The load-bearing constraint: it is what makes the transfer claim mechanically true rather than asserted. Implemented as a runtime assertion over named_parameters() against the node counts {10, 47, 49, 61, 7165}.

nodes.label: Node-indexed parameters eliminate most of the state of the art
nodes.rationale: One set of shared weights must run unchanged over graphs of 10/47/49/61/7,165 nodes across disjoint geographies. Graph WaveNet, MTGNN and AGCRN all carry a learned node-embedding dictionary E in R^{Nxd}, and EpiGNN a learnable W^s in R^{NxN} - parameters indexed by node, sized by N, therefore both untransferable and a direct disease tell. Cola-GNN, STAN, MepoGNN and CausalGNN are single-disease by construction or bake in compartmental parameters that violate disease-agnosticism if placed in the trunk.

nodes.label: PEMS (ICLR 2024) and CAPE (2025) - the closest transferable prior art
nodes.rationale: They prove cross-disease pre-training works but are purely temporal with no spatial encoder. An inductive spatial channel over a shared temporal trunk is precisely the unoccupied cell, and it is the contribution.

nodes.label: BLOCKER - Ebola has zero support origins under the frozen protocol
nodes.rationale: Support is a calendar prefix through 2014-05-24 = week index 7, so all 27 support cells lie in t in [0,7]; origins() requires t >= 19 and t+15 <= 51, so the earliest target cell is t+3 = 22. The sets are disjoint and the inner loop has nothing to supervise on. Resolution: separate the adaptation protocol from the evaluation protocol, since only the latter is frozen - left-pad short windows for adaptation only, accept that h=10 and h=15 admit no support target under any windowing choice, and reframe the headline as zero-shot with light short-horizon adaptation, which is both the honest framing and the stronger claim given 52 of 61 districts are zero-shot regardless.

nodes.label: TemporalEncoder - dilated causal TCN, shared and inductive
nodes.rationale: The Graph-WaveNet temporal block with the adaptive-adjacency machinery removed: 5 layers, dilations [1,2,4,8,16], kernel 2, gated activation, residual and skip connections, d=64. Nodes go into the batch dimension, so the module is node-count-agnostic for free and satisfies C2 trivially. Chosen over a recurrent trunk partly because Week-4 MAML inner loops backpropagate through the adaptation step, and doing that through a recurrent net over 20 timesteps is where memory and wall-clock die.

nodes.label: Receptive-field assertion (RF >= lookback)
nodes.rationale: An earlier draft specified kernel 2 with dilations [1,2,4], which is RF 8 - it would have silently ignored 60 per cent of the lookback window while training, converging and producing plausible numbers. Asserted at construction as rf = 1 + sum((k-1)*d), with a paired negative control requiring [1,2,4] to fail.

nodes.label: SpatialMixer - inductive, mask-aware message passing
nodes.rationale: Self-loop before normalisation (never invert D from A alone - four influenza nodes have degree 0 and will produce NaN); aggregation renormalised over observed neighbours only, because Ebola reporting is sparse and smoothing over unobserved neighbours propagates reporting artefacts as epidemiological signal; GraphSAGE-style separate self and neighbour weights, both d x d with no N anywhere. A node with no observed neighbours falls back to its self-loop, which the identity guarantees exists.

nodes.label: The learned spatial gate (a contribution, not plumbing)
nodes.rationale: g = sigmoid(MLP(h)), a per-node scalar from a small d -> d/4 -> 1 MLP, so data-dependent, inductive and C2-clean; h_out = (1-g)h + g*h_spatial. Three reasons: graceful degradation, since if geography is uninformative g -> 0 and the encoder collapses to the graph-free forecaster so the spatial channel can only help; defect mitigation, since the dengue topology is known mis-specified; and reportability - but not as raw g, which is not scale-free because a model can reach identical effective mixing with g=0.2 and a large-norm spatial branch. Report the norm-normalised spatial contribution instead and keep raw g as a debug metric.

nodes.label: Adaptation surface - FiLM modulation plus head (~388 params)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately tiny: Ebola's 27 support cells yield very few usable adaptation origins and none at h=10/15, so a few hundred parameters can move but cannot possibly discover a transmission topology. The burden of learning structure sits in pre-training and graph construction, never in the inner loop. Build the shared_params()/adaptation_params() split now so Week 4 is a training-loop change only.

nodes.label: Quantile head with pinball loss, superseding the point head
nodes.rationale: invert_scaler is expm1(sigma*z + mu), strictly monotone, and quantiles are equivariant under monotone transforms, so a predicted 95th percentile in model space inverts to exactly the 95th percentile in count space. A Gaussian's mean and variance do not survive expm1 - the inverted distribution is log-normal and the closed-form CRPS no longer applies. Since Week 5 needs CRPS, PICP and interval width in count space, the quantile head makes every uncertainty number exact by construction. Linear(d -> |H| x |Q|) emits all four horizons x five levels in one pass; the median is the point forecast.

nodes.label: Window normalisation dropped - the released scaler is already per-node
nodes.rationale: fit_scalers_masked returns mean/std of shape [N], so X[:,:,0] arrives at the trunk already log1p + per-node z-scored; adding a RevIN-style window norm would double-normalise, distort the sin/cos channels' relative amplitude, and collide with the per-origin refit. It resolves the earlier concern in an unexpected direction: cross-node magnitude is already gone, and gone by necessity - node-level magnitude is a proxy for population, hence geography, hence disease identity, which C1 forbids. The spatial channel therefore transports phase and shape co-movement, not magnitude gradients: real signal, since wave propagation is a timing phenomenon, but a narrower claim the manuscript must make. Only the node-level-mean variance diagnostic is retained.

nodes.label: Topology-robust pre-training (edge dropout, rewiring)
nodes.rationale: Perturb the graph every origin so the encoder never learns to trust a single topology; it is explicitly trained for graph mis-specification, which is the Ebola condition and, per the audit, the dengue condition too. Never perturb at evaluation. Anneal p_drop linearly 0 -> 0.3 over the first 30 per cent of training so the gate learns on a trustworthy graph before robustness pressure arrives.

nodes.label: The gate x augmentation 2x2 (the primary ablation)
nodes.rationale: Augmentation and the gate are in direct tension and can cancel: under aggressive augmentation the optimal policy is g -> 0 everywhere, because the encoder learns the graph is unreliable precisely because you made it unreliable, and the paper's two novel components neutralise each other. Two separate one-way ablations cannot distinguish 'augmentation helps' from 'augmentation suppressed the gate and the temporal trunk carried the result', so the primary table is {gate on, g=0} x {topo-aug none, edge_drop} at 5 seeds per cell.

nodes.label: Encoder test gates, each with a paired negative control
nodes.rationale: Mirrors the Phase-2 discipline: a gate that cannot fail proves nothing. Covers no node-indexed params, size agnosticism, isolated-node finiteness, no covariates, masked loss, per-origin scaler refit, permutation equivariance, no rollout, gate-nests-graph-free, receptive field, and normalisation round-trip - each with a planted defect the gate must catch.

nodes.label: What permutation equivariance does and does not prove
nodes.rationale: It proves node-order independence, not disease-agnosticism. The encoder can still infer which pathogen it is looking at from N, graph density, seasonal amplitude and mask sparsity, none of which any test removes. The defensible claim is narrower and exactly two things - no static covariate reaches the trunk, and no parameter is node-indexed - which is disease-agnosticism at the parameterisation level, not the information level. Concede it explicitly, or a reviewer will write 'the model can identify the pathogen from dynamics alone' and be right.

nodes.label: Multi-relational spatial input deferred - single-relation is forced
nodes.rationale: Parallel channels over contiguity / distance-decay / k-NN with attention over relations is the principled answer to kernel mis-specification, but a distance-decay adjacency is a new artifact absent from the frozen bundles and would need a gated addition to the build plus per-graph edge-weight normalisation so absolute scale cannot act as a disease tell. Meanwhile bundles.Bundle has no A_mob field at all, so single-relation mixing is forced by data availability rather than chosen - say so explicitly in the limitations, because silence here reads as oversight.

nodes.label: Shuffled-adjacency negative control
nodes.rationale: Performance must degrade on dengue; if it does not, the spatial channel is decorative and that must be reported honestly.

nodes.label: Decision thresholds that change the plan
nodes.rationale: If the spatial channel adds less than 2-3 per cent over a temporal-only baseline on Ebola few-shot, demote spatial mixing to a light residual, lead with the temporal trunk, and open the multi-relational work. If dengue OOMs after all three memory fallbacks, drop to STGCN-style Chebyshev K <= 2.

nodes.label: Memory budget and fallback order on the 12 GB card
nodes.rationale: Full-graph forward is comfortable at [7165, 20, 64] fp32 (~37 MB per activation) provided A stays a sparse COO tensor; densifying a 7,165^2 matrix is 205 MB fp32 alone and will end the run. Fallbacks in order: gradient checkpointing on the TCN, neighbour sampling over dengue only, then d=48.

nodes.label: C8 - Ebola never enters model selection
nodes.rationale: All encoder hyperparameters are selected on development validation folds and adaptation settings by leave-one-development-disease-out, then frozen; Ebola's query set is scored once with a fixed number of adaptation steps and no early stopping on query, and carries no validation split by design. Any code path that reads an Ebola metric before the final run is a correctness bug, and test_ebola_never_in_selection exists to catch it.
